clue.text: Healthy American eating a Japanese dish

indicators.note: whatever eats something takes it inside itself, so one string of letters goes within another

blocks.note: fit means in good health
A is a standard abbreviation for American
taken as written
J is the abbreviation for Japanese

explanation.surface: A health-conscious American tucks into some sushi or similar Japanese food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Japanese dish' reads as one phrase, but the Japanese contributes only its J; FIT plus A swallows A and J to give F-AJ-ITA.
explanation.definitionFit: A fajita is a Mexican-style food of grilled meat strips wrapped in a tortilla, so it is one particular kind of dish.

clue.text: Over the top of muesli, mostly nuts

indicators.note: mostly means not all of it, so the final letter is dropped
nuts means crazy, so the letters go wild and are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
the breakfast cereal minus its last letter

explanation.surface: A breakfast bowl heaped with a topping that is mostly nuts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' looks like a joining word but is part of the fodder; OF plus MUESL rearranges to the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Fulsome praise is excessive and flattering to the point of insincerity, which is what over the top describes.

clue.text: Trip one's taken to the south exposing dictatorship

indicators.note: in a down answer the south is the bottom, so this letter is moved to the end

blocks.note: a jaunt is a short trip; its A is lifted out to be moved
A is one, as in 'a' meaning one thing

explanation.surface: A journey abroad that reveals the reality of an authoritarian regime.
explanation.walkthrough: JAUNT has its A moved from second place down to the bottom of the light, making JUNTA.
explanation.definitionFit: A junta is a military group ruling a country after seizing power, a form of government without elections.

clue.text: Mistake on documents masks hospital's condition

indicators.note: a mask covers something up, so one set of letters hides another inside
in a down clue, being on something means sitting above it, so this goes first

blocks.note: a typo is a typing mistake
H is the map and sign abbreviation for hospital
ID is identity documents

explanation.surface: A clerical error in paperwork conceals a patient's medical diagnosis.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above, so the mistake with its hidden letter sits over the papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Typhoid is a serious bacterial fever, so it is a medical condition in the sense of an illness.

clue.text: Beginning to justify mate's untidy stuff getting washed up

indicators.note: the beginning of a word is its opening letter only
something untidy is messed about, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: first letter of the word
the letters of the word, apostrophe ignored

explanation.surface: Someone tries to excuse a friend's messy belongings being cleaned up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'washed up' suggests dishes after a meal; here it is the sea depositing things on the shore.
explanation.definitionFit: Jetsam is cargo thrown overboard from a ship that later drifts ashore, so it is material the tide deposits on beaches.

clue.text: Refer to Skinny being upset? It makes you sick!

indicators.note: upset means turned over, and in a down answer that sends the letters upward

blocks.note: to cite a source is to refer to it
Skinny is the setter, who calls themself me

explanation.surface: Mention the setter being upset, and the reply is that it is sickening.
explanation.walkthrough: Skinny is this puzzle's setter, so the name stands for ME. CITE ME read upward gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: An emetic is a substance taken to induce vomiting, so it is a thing which causes nausea and throwing up.

clue.text: Out of form son unlucky to take English

indicators.note: to take in something is to accept it inside, so a letter goes into the word

blocks.note: S is the genealogical abbreviation for son
hapless means unfortunate
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: A footballer's son is playing badly and has bad luck with the English side.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of form' sounds like a sportsman playing poorly, but it is taken literally: lacking a shape. E goes into HAPLESS after S.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without form has no definite outline or structure, the literal sense of lacking a shape.

clue.text: Camera shot captures front of military craft ...

indicators.note: shot means ruined or broken, so the letters are knocked out of order
to capture is to hold inside, so one set of letters goes round another
the front of a word is just its first letter

blocks.note: taken as written
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A camera takes a picture of the bow of a warship, continuing into the next clue.
explanation.walkthrough: 'military craft' looks like a warship, but 'craft' alone is the definition, meaning a handicraft. CAMERA rearranged around M gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Macrame is the decorative art of knotting cord or string into patterns, a traditional handicraft hobby.

clue.text: ... support vessel in one's flotilla?

blocks.note: first meaning: the comfort of having others around
second meaning, whimsical: a boat sailing alongside as your mate, split into two words

explanation.surface: Continuing 7: a supply ship travelling as part of a naval group.
explanation.walkthrough: The ellipsis links the clue to the warship picture of 7, but the clues are separate; the question mark flags that the second definition splits the answer into two words.
explanation.definitionFit: Companionship is fellowship and friendly presence, which gives emotional support to someone who might otherwise be lonely.

clue.text: Work out half of 4? Not quite

indicators.note: not quite all of it means the final letter falls away

blocks.note: 4-across is JETSAM; its first half is JET, which is a kind of aircraft

explanation.surface: Someone tries to calculate half of four and doesn't quite manage it.
explanation.walkthrough: The 4 is a cross-reference to 4-across, not a number: JETSAM split in half gives JET, a plane, which is then cut short to PLAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To plan something is to devise or arrange it in advance, just as working out a scheme means deciding how it will happen.

clue.text: Established champion claims northern origin

indicators.note: to claim is to take hold of something, so one letter is held within

blocks.note: something proven has been established as true
an ace is an expert or champion
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A long-standing title-holder insists they come from the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'claims northern origin' reads like someone asserting roots, but it is ACE taking in N.
explanation.definitionFit: Provenance is the place or source something comes from, especially the documented history of an artwork or antique.

clue.text: Fruit characterised by overly dull jams

indicators.note: to jam is to squeeze something into a space, so one word is packed inside another

blocks.note: too means excessively
mat, also spelt matt, means without shine

explanation.surface: A fruit known for producing jams that are far too bland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jams' sits naturally beside fruit as preserves, but here it is a verb meaning squeezes in.
explanation.definitionFit: Botanically the tomato is a fruit, since it is the seed-bearing part of the plant, though often cooked as a vegetable.

clue.text: Ancient vampire bats fly without wings

indicators.note: bats means crazy, so these letters are scrambled
losing its wings means losing both outside letters, leaving only the middle

blocks.note: taken as written
the word minus its first and last letters

explanation.surface: Old vampire bats that cannot fly because they have lost their wings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'vampire bats' reads as the animal, but 'bats' is the anagram signal; 'fly' gives just its middle letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Primeval describes the earliest ages of the world, so it means extremely old or primordial.

clue.text: Insisting on something being difficult

blocks.note: first meaning: asking for something firmly as a right
second meaning: requiring a lot of effort or skill

explanation.surface: Someone stubbornly holding out for something and making life hard.
explanation.walkthrough: One word serving as both a verb form and an adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Demanding is both the participle of demand, to insist firmly, and an adjective for tasks that are hard and taxing.

clue.text: Like I said regularly - two people, you and I - hard-working

indicators.note: at regular intervals means every other letter is kept

blocks.note: as means like, as in 'white as snow'
second and fourth letters of the phrase
a duo is a pair
you and I together are us

explanation.surface: A speaker insisting that a couple, themself and the listener, are diligent workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Like I said' reads as one casual phrase, but 'Like' stands alone and 'I said' is the fodder for the regular letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Assiduous means showing great care, persistence and diligence, the qualities of a person who toils hard.

clue.text: Abandon children, so it's said

indicators.note: something said is spoken, so a word that only sounds right is wanted

blocks.note: seed is an old word for offspring or descendants

explanation.surface: Deserting one's own kids, or so people claim.
explanation.walkthrough: Seed means offspring, as in the biblical 'Abraham and his seed'.
explanation.definitionFit: To cede territory or a right is to give it up or surrender it to another, a form of relinquishing.

clue.text: Discharge with hard shove

blocks.note: pus is the discharge from an infected wound
H is the pencil abbreviation for hard

explanation.surface: Firing someone with a rough physical shove out the door.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Discharge' suggests dismissal or firing a gun; here it is the medical sense.
explanation.definitionFit: To push and to shove are synonyms, both meaning to press against something forcefully to move it away.

clue.text: Worry as forward with United starts to run backwards

indicators.note: the starts of words are their opening letters

blocks.note: pert means cheeky or forward
U is the abbreviation for United in team names
first letters of the two words

explanation.surface: Fans fret as a United striker starts running the wrong way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forward' and 'United' paint a football picture; forward actually means impudent, and 'backwards' is only fodder for its initial, not a reversal.
explanation.definitionFit: To perturb someone is to unsettle or disturb them, causing anxiety, which is what making them worry means.

clue.text: Complete housing project by centre of picturesque UK city

indicators.note: to house is to give shelter inside, so one word goes within another
the centre of a word is its middle letter

blocks.note: done means finished
to project is to throw or cast
the sixth of eleven letters

explanation.surface: A finished housing scheme beside the pretty historic centre of a British city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'housing project' looks like a building scheme but splits into an indicator and a verb. DONCASTER is a town in South Yorkshire, England, granted city status in 2022.
explanation.definitionFit: Doncaster became a city in 2022 as part of the Platinum Jubilee civic honours, so it fits a British urban place.

clue.text: 25's clothes

definitions.note: refers to 25-across, WHAM, a verb meaning to hit

blocks.note: first meaning: the answer to 25-across, to hit hard
second meaning: British slang for clothing and gear

explanation.walkthrough: The cross-reference leads to WHAM, a verb meaning to strike; clobber is also informal British slang for one's clothes and belongings.
explanation.definitionFit: To clobber is to hit someone heavily, matching a violent wallop, and as a noun it means a person's outfit or kit.

clue.text: Country's aim - installing good network

indicators.note: to install is to put something in place inside, so letters are fitted within

blocks.note: an end is a goal or purpose
G is the abbreviation for good
a LAN is a local area network

explanation.surface: A nation's goal is to set up a decent broadband system.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's is read as 'is' joining the definition to the wordplay: END takes in G and LAN.
explanation.definitionFit: England is one of the constituent nations of the United Kingdom, a land with its own national identity.

clue.text: Marry after extremely regrettable service

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its two end letters
coming after means placed second in the sequence

blocks.note: first and last letters of the word
to pair is to join two together, as in a wedding

explanation.surface: Getting wed after a dreadful ceremony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' looks like the wedding ceremony, but it is the garage sense: maintenance work.
explanation.definitionFit: To service a car or machine is to inspect and mend it, so service and repair overlap as maintenance work.

clue.text: Lack of moisture in canned sardines

indicators.note: canned food is processed and packed, so these letters are reworked into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Tinned fish that have gone dry, a common complaint.
explanation.walkthrough: Canned sardines are sold in oil, so a dry tin makes a wry joke; 'canned' is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Aridness is the state of being arid, extremely dry, so it describes an absence of water or dampness.

clue.text: Good lord! See, on retiring, one's second childhood

indicators.note: retiring means going back or withdrawing, so the letters travel backwards

blocks.note: egad is an old exclamation of surprise
lo is an archaic word meaning look or see

explanation.surface: An exclamation on retirement: life after work is like being a child again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retiring' suggests leaving work, which fits the surface about ageing, but here it signals the letters going back.
explanation.definitionFit: A second childhood is an idiom for the later years of life, when someone may become dependent or carefree again.

clue.text: With spades gathered, should you and I look for water?

indicators.note: something gathered is collected in, so a letter is taken inside

blocks.note: the question form of 'should we': 'do we'
S is the card abbreviation for spades

explanation.surface: Having fetched our shovels, shall the two of us dig for a well?
explanation.walkthrough: 'spades' fits the digging picture, but it is the card suit giving S, which goes inside DO WE.
explanation.definitionFit: To dowse is to search for underground water using a divining rod, which is exactly a way to seek a spring.

clue.text: Forbidden city in Italy (in Italy!), overthrown, initially being isolated

indicators.note: overthrown means turned upside down, so the letters run the other way
initially means at the start, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: out means not allowed, as in 'that's out'
the Lombard city's name as Italians spell it
first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A city in Italy banned after a coup, left cut off from the rest.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracketed '(in Italy!)' asks for the local spelling: Milan becomes MILANO, which then reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Out on a limb is an idiom for being alone in a risky or unsupported position, cut off from others.

clue.text: London team, not established club

indicators.note: not having something means it is taken out

blocks.note: West Ham United is a London football club
EST is the abbreviation for established, seen on shop signs

explanation.surface: A London side that is not a well-established football club.
explanation.walkthrough: 'club' looks like a football club, matching the London team, but it is a verb meaning to hit. West Ham is a Premier League football club from east London.
explanation.definitionFit: To club someone is to strike them with a heavy object, and wham is a forceful blow or to hit hard.

clue.text: Pen 40% of story inside restaurant

indicators.note: forty per cent of five letters is two, so only the opening pair is kept
inside means within, so one piece sits in the middle of another

blocks.note: a Biro is a ballpoint pen
first letters of the word, two of its five, which is forty per cent

explanation.surface: Writing part of a tale while sitting in a café.
explanation.walkthrough: Biro is the everyday British name for a ballpoint pen, from its inventor László Bíró.
explanation.definitionFit: A bistro is a small, informal French-style eatery serving simple meals, a type of dining establishment.

clue.text: Familiar way to have eggs - including a dash of nutmeg

indicators.note: a dash is a tiny amount, so just one opening letter is used
to include is to contain, so a letter goes inside

blocks.note: fried is one way eggs are cooked
first letter of the spice

explanation.surface: A well-known recipe for eggs with a sprinkle of nutmeg.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Familiar' reads as an adjective meaning well-known, but it is a noun: a familiar is an intimate companion.
explanation.definitionFit: A familiar, in the old sense, is a close associate or intimate companion, which is a close acquaintance.
